chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarri, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'I travel in this direction, and sometimes there is no place where I can pray due to the snow.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is possible for you not to prostrate on the snow, then do not prostrate; and if it is not possible for you, then level it and prostrate upon it.'
And in another hadith: 'Prostrate upon your garment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prostrating on snow during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) illustrates the principle of *al-khuruj min al-dar' ila al-aslah* (moving from the more difficult to the easier) in Shia fiqh, prioritizing the preservation of the prayer's validity over ideal conditions. It highlights the practical flexibility granted to worshippers in harsh environments, allowing for prostration on leveled snow or one's garment when direct contact with the earth is compromised. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) while maintaining the essential requirement of prostrating on a pure, natural surface.
